focus_primary_path.instructions: Given `screen.purpose`, how obvious is the main thing to do in the images?

criteria.what: Several controls compete for attention, or nothing shows what to do first
examples: Four filled buttons in different colors in the header
A promo banner, a tour popup, and a filled button all ask for a click

criteria.what: A main action exists, but other strong buttons, banners, or promotions compete with it
examples: A filled 'Create' button next to a filled 'Upgrade' button of the same size

criteria.what: One main path is obvious: one filled button whose label names the job of the screen, or the job is to pick an item from the content and no control competes with it
examples: An agents list where only 'Create Agent' is a filled dark button
A thread list where the rows are the focus and the header has only text buttons

focus_affordance.instructions: In the images, can the user tell which elements are actions and which are static text?

criteria.what: Actions and static text look the same
examples: A header row where a branch name, a path, and 'Rename branch' all use the same plain text style

criteria.what: Most actions look clickable, but some look like labels or labels look like buttons
examples: Buttons have borders, but one text action in the header has no style

criteria.what: Every action looks clickable through a button shape, an icon, a link color, or a chevron, and static text never does
examples: 'Filters' and 'Display' are text buttons with icons and shortcut hints, and the page title is plain bold text

status_items.instructions: In the images, how well does each item show its current state without the user opening it?

criteria.what: Items show no state; the user must open each item to learn it
examples: A list of project names with no status, owner, or date

criteria.what: Some items show state, or state uses color only, with no icon, label, or count
examples: Rows have a colored left border but no label

criteria.what: Each item that can change shows its state inline with an icon, a label, or a count
examples: Sidebar threads show a spinner while running and a 'Needs input' badge when blocked
Each queue in the sidebar shows a count, such as 'First response 4'
A project chip shows 'On track' with a green icon

status_consistent.instructions: In the images, do all status signals agree, with no spinner or running sign next to a label that says the work is stopped, sleeping, or done?

status_lifecycle.instructions: In the images, when work or a workspace is sleeping, paused, or stopped, how does the screen explain it?

criteria.explains: It names the state and says how to resume, such as 'Message Claude Code to wake this workspace'
criteria.bare: It names the state, but does not say what it means or how to resume
criteria.not_shown: Nothing in the images is sleeping, paused, or stopped

nav_current.instructions: Do the images show which navigation item is the current location, with a visible selected state?

nav_groups.instructions: In the images, how is the navigation organized?
criteria: One long flat list, or items with no clear groups
Groups exist, but names are vague or items repeat
Short groups with clear names, such as pinned items, recent items by day, records, or workflow states, with counts where they help

nav_return.instructions: In the images, can the user go back to recent or pinned work from the navigation in one click?

nav_tabs_current.instructions: In the images, how clearly does the active tab differ from the other tabs?

criteria.clear: The active tab has a clear mark, such as a different background, an underline, or bold text
criteria.weak: The active tab differs only by a small change in text color

speed_search.instructions: Do the images show search or a command menu, such as a search field or a '⌘K' hint?

speed_shortcuts.instructions: In the images, do frequent actions show their keyboard shortcut next to the label, such as 'Filters F'?

copy_labels.instructions: How clear are the words in the images and in `page_text`?
criteria: Vague, clever, or jargon words; buttons say 'Submit', 'OK', or 'Click here'
Mostly clear, with some vague labels or mixed capitalization
Plain, specific words; buttons start with a verb that names the result, such as 'Post update' or 'Add billing'; capitalization is consistent

copy_status.instructions: In the images, do status labels use plain words that a new user understands, such as 'Waiting for customer' or 'On track'?

copy_controls_labeled.instructions: In the images, does every dropdown, toggle, and selector show what it sets, through a label, an icon, or a value that explains itself?

states_disabled_clear.instructions: In the images, can the user tell disabled controls from enabled controls?

criteria.clear: Disabled controls look clearly faded, and enabled controls never look faded
criteria.confusing: Some enabled controls look faded or disabled, or disabled controls look active
criteria.not_shown: The images show no disabled controls

icons_one_set.instructions: Do the images use one icon set, with the same style and stroke weight everywhere?

icons_size.instructions: In the images, do icons have one size in each context, and do they sit centered with their labels?

icons_meaning.instructions: In the images, how clear are the icon-only buttons?
criteria: Icons are unusual or abstract, and they have no labels
Most icons are common symbols, but some are unclear
Every icon-only button is a common symbol, such as search, close, or add, or it has a label

quality_tiny_text.instructions: In the images, is navigation, link, control, or body text set very small?
